text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Russia agrees to pay French holders of tsarist-era debt a total of up to two billion francs, settling a dispute that had blocked trade in a new Russian bond in France, and allowing Russia to consider joining the Paris Club. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).

-- Mediator in conflict between truck drivers and employers may resign for lack of real negotiating power, while petrol supplies decrease and strikers tighten blockade of towns and petrol depots. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).
-- Compagnie des Machines Bull to be privatised before end December, current shareholders Nec, Motorola and France Telecom are expected to increase their stakes.

-- GEC chairman Lord Weinstock reaffirms GEC is interested in Thomson, calls in an interview for a merger of its subsidiary Marconi with Thomson-CSF to achieve economies of scale and a good product mix.
-- UAP vice-chairman Didier Pfeiffer expected to replace Jean-Jacques Bonnaud as GAN chairman, government to issue decree replacing Bonnaud today.
-- Repairs from Eurotunnel fire may take three to five months.
-- Consortium de Realisation, a structure selling off Credit Lyonnais assets, makes a 4.5 billion franc first-half loss and expects to have sold some 40 billion francs worth of assets in 1996.
-- Bourse watchdog COB launches probe into Lagardere share moves on the eve of last month's announcement that Lagardere was the preferred candidate to buy Thomson .
-- Labour Minister Jacques Barrot considers labour flexibility policy with caution, for some economic sectors.
-- A planned reshuffle of hospital organisation, with the creation of regional hospital centers, may trigger closing of some partially operated hospitals.
-- UAP says its maximum exposure to an insurance claim from the Eurotunnel consortium after last week's fire would be 75 million francs.
